TM601_LS_RDSON.verdict: rule applies; 3 of 4 findings rest on false premises

findings.evidence: gate message: 'TM601_LS_RDSON: 静态供电 VBUS 但未闭稳压电容 K5_VBUS_Cap' (gate-logs-t20/relay-trace.log L8). The only source of VBUS in powered_pins is hardwareInit {"cmd":"vset","pin":"vbus","value":5.0} in project/DALI/meta/dali_tm_meta.json -> functions[TM601_LS_RDSON]. BD-08 defines that as simulationDomainReference; the payload sources only VBAT 4.2 / PMID 9 / VDRV 5 (payload:356,357,359,361) - no VBUS source. python-scanned test.cpp contains no VBUS source object (only relay names such as K5_VBUS_Cap and unrelated TM names). Schematic: VBUS is a floating-channel arrival point, not a supply: SCH-Connect-Map.txt:213 'CH0 Low -> VBUS ... K3', :214 'S1_FPVIe_FL0 -> K89(NC) -> K3(ON) -> K4(NC) -> VBUS_F'.
findings.impact: The gate demands closure of a bulk-cap relay on a rail that is not energised in this run; complying would add a 4.7 uF branch for no functional reason and would corrupt the forced-current measurement if the rail is tied to the floating channel.
findings.correction: Fix the model, not the code: drop VBUS from the run-scoped meta powered_pins (hardwareInit 'vset vbus' is simulation-domain), and remove K5_VBUS_Cap from the payload SetOn. Do NOT close K5 to make the gate green.
findings.verification: Re-run verify_relay_trace.py with the run-scoped meta: the K5_VBUS_Cap finding for TM601_LS_RDSON must disappear while no new finding appears; confirm VBUS absent from powered_pins by python read of the meta copy.

findings.evidence: gate messages L5/L6 read '静态供电 SW' for caps whose PIN tokens are SW1_BST1 and SW2_BST2. Mechanism reproduced with the gate's own logic: cap_pin('K45_Cap_SW1_BST1')='SW1_BST1', cap_pin('K44_Cap_SW2_BST2')='SW2_BST2', and fam_intersect({'ISW','SW','VBAT','VBUS','VDRV'},'SW1_BST1')={'SW'} because 'SW1_BST1'.startswith('SW'). SW1/SW2 are NOT declared in the meta powered_pins at all; they are separate rails reached only via K46 (SCH-Connect-Map.txt:177) and K46+K49 (:183), while this item routes SW via K60,K61 (:174) and PGND via K154,K155 (:156).
findings.impact: Two distinct rails (SW vs SW1/SW2) are folded into one family by name prefix, so any TM that powers SW triggers closure demands for the SW1/SW2 bootstrap caps. Reciprocally, an unpowered SW1/SW2 could mask a genuinely required closure.
findings.correction: Make the family match token-boundary aware (require p == fam or p.startswith(fam + '_')) OR stop declaring SW1_BST1/SW2_BST2 as members of the SW family in the meta. Scope the change to this run first; if the shared script is changed, land it only after a sandbox before/after comparison because fam_intersect is called at L318/L321/L325 and in the degraded branch L394.
findings.verification: With the tightened match, enumerate required closures for TM601_LS_RDSON and confirm K44/K45 drop out while K13/K57 remain; enumerate for the whole tree under --src sandbox to confirm no previously-satisfied function becomes newly red.

findings.evidence: TM601_LS_RDSON declares mi_pins=[] and ramp_pins=[] while its hardwareInit contains iset pmid_sw 1.0 (a forced 1 A current path). The rule's exemption at L325 compares the CAP's own token - for K57_CAP_BST_SW that token is BST_SW (cap_pin at L100-116), not SW - so the exemption cannot fire. The fields are demonstrably usable elsewhere: 27/101 functions populate mi_pins and 41/101 populate ramp_pins, including TM641_BST_UV.ramp_pins=['SW'] and TM1009_QDT_VPCHG_SHORT_CURRENT.mi_pins=['SW1'].
findings.impact: The item cannot express 'this pin carries the forced measurement current', so the gate falls back to demanding the static-power closure rule for a pin that is in the measurement loop.
findings.correction: Declare the forced-current / ramp pins explicitly for TM601_LS_RDSON in the run-scoped meta (minimal, exact token set). CAUTION measured: declaring 'PMID_SW' has NO collateral here (fam_intersect with the TM601 powered set returns [] for PMID_SW/PMID/PMIDSW), but this must be re-checked per token before adding, because the same prefix logic can over-match other families.
findings.verification: After adding the declaration, python-assert that the exemption fires for exactly the intended caps and that no other cap family loses its required closure.

findings.evidence: At the time of first inspection the payload's SetOn list read 'K154_BUSH0_AMUX, K155_FOVI3_PGND, K60_BUSL0_VCP, K61_ACM8_SW, K13_VBAT_Cap, K85_CAP_PMID, K57_CAP_BST_SW, K44_Cap_SW2_BST2, K45_Cap_SW1_BST1, K5_VBUS_Cap, K126_V1P5_CAP'. It closed K5_VBUS_Cap (an unpowered rail per T22-01) while NOT closing K3_BUSL0_VBUS, the relay that actually reaches VBUS (SCH-Connect-Map.txt:213) - i.e. a relay switched in purely to satisfy the gate, on no electrical path. During this review the implementer revised the payload (18:36:18, sha256 7399598332fac6c342ec44f2e0217e5f43cebc499e17974e4b8c431aded1885b) to remove K5/K44/K45 and to withdraw that rationale in a comment.
findings.impact: Closing a cap relay on an unpowered node adds no function, adds relay actuation and contact-path risk on a shared _S1S2 family, and can corrupt the forced-current measurement if that rail is tied to the floating channel. The revised payload still is not written to the target tree.
findings.correction: Keep K5/K44/K45 OUT of the TM601 SetOn list (as the 18:36 revision does). Fix the false premises at the model level (T22-01..03) instead of silencing the gate with closures. Never edit scripts/gate_baseline.json to mask this.
findings.verification: Confirm the deployed ForCodexDebug/source/test.cpp TM601_LS_RDSON SetOn list contains K57_CAP_BST_SW and K126_V1P5_CAP but none of K5_VBUS_Cap / K44_Cap_SW2_BST2 / K45_Cap_SW1_BST1 and no bare 126, then re-run the gate.

findings.evidence: Deployed file = 462848 B / python-plaintext sha256 3dbceb496d79d7d08631713b98e46c0c2ba6163eaf5356a87dded677e35ba479 / mtime 18:23:31. Its TM601_LS_RDSON SetOn (line 9197) reads 'K154_BUSH0_AMUX, K155_FOVI3_PGND, K60_BUSL0_VCP, K61_ACM8_SW, K13_VBAT_Cap, K85_CAP_PMID, 126' - missing the four caps and using a bare 126. The gate log (mtime 18:27:08) therefore evaluated 18:23:31 code, while the fixed payload was revised at 18:33:33 and again at 18:36:18. The write has never landed.
findings.impact: The recorded 4 FR-001 findings describe a superseded code state; equally, claims that those findings are 'gone' cannot be verified in the target tree. The bare 126 is a separate, unrelated ERROR class (fictional relay name) and is what actually makes the gate exit non-zero.
findings.correction: Write the final payload to the target tree as its own approved write task, then re-run the gate against the deployed state and re-record the log with the new hash.
findings.verification: python-plaintext sha256 of the deployed test.cpp changes from 3dbceb49..., and the re-run relay-trace log shows 0 errors and no FR-001 finding for TM601_LS_RDSON other than those registered by exception.

findings.evidence: The four TM601 capacitor items are appended to warns (L328), not errors. sys.exit(1) happens only under 'if errors' (L416-420); warns cause failure only with --warn-as-error (L237, L421-423). The gate log's '*** FAIL ***' (L9) is produced by the two '虚构继电器名 126 (无 #define)' errors (L10-11).
findings.impact: Treating the four capacitor items as the cause of the gate failure mis-attributes the failure and can misdirect the repair.
findings.correction: Record the two classes separately in the run ledger: (a) 4 FR-001 warnings (3 false positives + 1 true requirement already satisfied in the revised payload); (b) 2 fictional-relay-name errors causing exit 1.
findings.verification: Read the gate log's FAIL/WARNINGS sections and the exit path in verify_relay_trace.py:412-423.

plainAnswers.reasoning: The rule's own premise is 'this pin is statically powered' (L318-320). For VBUS that premise is factually false in this run (no VBUS source object in test.cpp; VBUS is a floating-channel arrival point at SCH-Connect-Map.txt:213/214/421). The payload at the time of inspection had added K5_VBUS_Cap to satisfy the gate while K3, the relay that actually reaches VBUS, was not closed - so the closure served no circuit. Counter-evidence inside the rule itself: L321 and L325 exist precisely to suppress needless closures. The correct fixes are a run-scoped model correction (T22-01..03) or a named, in-writing exception - never an electrically baseless SetOn, and never editing gate_baseline.json.
plainAnswers.doesThemeasuredCurrentPathExemptionCover: NO - not as written, and not in this item
plainAnswers.k57Ruling: K57_CAP_BST_SW is required to be closed for TM601_LS_RDSON, but NOT because of the SW-measured-current argument: the exemption at L325 tests the cap's own token BST_SW, and BST_SW is genuinely statically powered (hardwareInit bst_sw 5.0, and BST_SW is explicitly in powered_pins). The correct statement is 'do not close K57 blindly' - close it because its rail is really powered - and equally do not delete it to make the gate green. Settling/isolation effect of the 220 nF branch on the measured rail is not analysed here and is a bring-up (U11) item, consistent with the payload comment at :361-364.
